title: The Thorn of the Weeping Wood
premise: Ansel Voss, the only cartographer who can chart the shifting smuggler roads through the Thornfell mountains, inherits a dying stranger's map — one that leads to the Weeping Wood and the court beneath it, where souls are bought and sold as currency. The stranger's soul was the payment; his sister, Maren, is next to be collected unless Ansel can steal it back within nine nights. Guided by a disgraced ex-warden of the court who betrayed it long ago, Ansel discovers her own name already inked in the court's ledger: she was sold as an infant, and her survival has been borrowed time all along. In the end, Ansel trades her mapped knowledge of every hidden road for Maren's freedom, erasing herself from all maps — mortal and fae alike — and walks out of Thornfell unnamed, finally owning the life no one paid for.
about_author: Quentin Kavanagh is a former trail surveyor who spent six years mapping passes in the Carpathians before turning to fiction full-time. His novels blend precise geographic realism with folklore-dark fantasy, and he writes from a cabin he refuses to put on any map.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Ink
chapters.summary: Ansel Voss finishes a commission in the border town of Greyhollow when a bloodied stranger collapses at her door, pressing a folded map into her hands and whispering 'nine nights' before dying. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation — she wants to burn the map, but the man's terror won't let her.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Following the map's first road, Ansel is ambushed by hollow-eyed collectors who call her 'the collateral' and mark her hand with an ink-sigil. A scarred stranger, Corvin, drives them off and reveals the court beneath the mountain keeps a ledger of sold souls — and hers is in it. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: dread curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: Nine Nights on the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Corvin, once a warden of the court before his betrayal, bargains his way into partnership: he knows the court's weaknesses; only Ansel can navigate the roads that shift like weather. They travel together through Thornfell's passes. POV: alternating Ansel and Corvin. Emotional beat: wary trust built over shared firelight.

chapters.title: The Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: They reach the forest where trees bleed sap like tears and the dead stranger's memories surface in Ansel's dreams — including his face among the court's wardens. She realizes he sold himself to buy his sister Maren nine nights of grace. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: grief and guilt entwining; the mission becomes personal.

chapters.title: Tollgate of Teeth
chapters.summary: At the wood's heart stands a tollgate guarded by the Ferryman's hounds, which demand a memory as passage. Ansel sacrifices her memory of her mother's face; Corvin secretly pays with his name. POV: dual. Emotional beat: the first true price of survival — and the first lie between them.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Descending into the cavernous court, Ansel poses as a soul-broker while Corvin distracts the wardens. She sees the ledger itself: thousands of names, her own entered the night she was born — sold by someone who loved her enough to pay, or so the clerk claims. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity; everything she believed about her orphanhood cracks.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Ansel finds Maren alive in the court's keeping, half-faded, and learns the truth: the dying stranger wasn't Maren's brother but her father, and Corvin was the warden who processed the sale — his 'betrayal' was selling them out years ago. POV: Maren, brief and ghostlike. Emotional beat: betrayal detonating; Ansel must decide whether vengeance or rescue matters more.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Roads
chapters.summary: Confronting Corvin, Ansel extracts his confession and his help: the court's power flows from its monopoly on hidden ways. She offers the Judge-King the one thing it cannot map — herself, the living key to every shifting road — in exchange for Maren's soul and erasure of both ledgers. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: cold clarity; justice outside any law, priced in self.

chapters.title: Where the Mountain Sings
chapters.summary: The court accepts — then reneges, moving to claim Ansel entirely. In the climax, she and Corvin flee through roads only she can read, collapsing passages behind them as the mountain howls; Corvin stays behind to hold the last gate, paying his debt in full. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: terror, sacrifice, and the fierce joy of outpacing fate.

chapters.title: Unmapped
chapters.summary: Above ground, Maren wakes whole and remembers nothing of the court; Ansel carries every memory and none of her old name, which died in the ledger. She draws one final map — a blank page — and gives it to Maren with directions to a life neither of them owes anyone. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; identity chosen, not purchased.
